title: Pruning for Efficiency, Paying in Fairness: Demographic Disparities in Pruned Speech-LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing Word Error Rate (WER) disparities among speakers of different ethnicities (e.g., Black, Asian, White, Hispanic) using the Fair-Speech dataset before and after model pruning.
Comparing Word Error Rate (WER) differences between male and female speakers using the Fair-Speech and Common Voice datasets.
Evaluating Word Error Rate (WER) disparities across different socioeconomic status groups (Low, Medium, Affluent) using the Fair-Speech dataset.
Measuring Word Error Rate (WER) performance gaps across various speaker age brackets (e.g., 18-22, 46-65) using the Fair-Speech and Common Voice datasets.

Comparing Word Error Rate (WER) across speakers with different regional accents (e.g., US, England, and Indian/South Asian for English; Netherlands vs. Belgian for Dutch) using the Common Voice datasets.
